chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a believer who kills a believer intentionally: is there repentance for him? He said:

If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or for some worldly cause, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If no one knew of it, he should go to the heirs of the slain and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he should give them the blood-money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty poor persons.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money; the financial compensation due to the heirs
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer; the victim and perpetrator are both identified as believers
key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: repentance; the possibility and conditions of returning from the sin
key_terms.لِإِيمَانِهِ: because of his faith; meaning the killing was motivated by the victim’s belief
key_terms.لِغَضَبٍ: out of anger; indicating an emotional motive rather than enmity to faith itself
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: a poor person; one of the recipients of the expiatory feeding
key_terms.يُقَادَ: that retribution be carried out; i.e., qiṣāṣ is taken from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repentance for a believer who intentionally kills another believer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling regarding one believer who intentionally kills another and distinguishes between killing out of hostility to faith and killing due to anger or worldly motives. It states that repentance in the latter case requires submitting to legal retribution or, if pardoned, fulfilling financial and expiatory obligations.
